summary.headline: Kansai Nerolac Q4 FY26 standalone revenue up 7.6% and PBDIT up 21%; management guides to 13-14% margin and high-single-digit decorative price increases.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone revenue grew 7.6% with PBDIT up 21% and PBT before exceptional items up 12.8%, while full-year standalone revenue rose 3.2% and PBDIT 1.2%. Consolidated Q4 PBDIT rose 30.6%. Management attributed the quarter's margin resilience to better mix in both decorative and industrial, and to lower other expenses. Price hikes totalling roughly 2% in March and 5-6% in each subsequent round were taken amid a crude and rupee shock tied to the West Asia crisis. The company said demand has held so far with no volume impact seen, but visibility for FY27 is "wait and watch."

segments.name: Decorative
segments.commentary: Management said the decorative volume-value gap was not significant, as low-profit items were deliberately curtailed. Growth in the decorative business was described as mid-single-digit or lower, and new products and super premium emulsions drove better mix. Decorative projects are now about 10%+ of sales, and new businesses (waterproofing, construction chemicals, wood finish) are also 10%+ and slightly higher than projects.

segments.name: Industrial - Automotive
segments.commentary: Auto coatings grew close to double digits in Q4, with passenger vehicle demand healthy and a long waiting list cited by customers. Two-wheeler demand grew at high double digits, and commercial vehicles and tractors grew at double digits.

segments.name: Industrial - General and Powder
segments.commentary: Overall industrial grew slightly higher single digits in Q4 per management. Powder coatings returned to mid-single-digit growth with a good channel sales performance.

guidance_outlook: Management reiterated the historical EBITDA margin band of 13-14% for FY27 on both consolidated and standalone bases, with an endeavour to reach the higher end. FY26 was said to have been within that range.

Decorative price increases: about 2% in late March, then 5-6% each on 10 April, 21 April and 11 May, for a net higher-single-digit increase as of now. Aniruddha Joshi's question put the cumulative effective hike in the low teens; management did not dispute it.
Industrial channel prices were revised effective mid-April. OE price increases have been granted in part, with negotiation timing slightly delayed but effective-from dates protecting margins.

Management said a crude price of about USD 100 would be manageable with current price hikes. It expects to live with the inflation for about 6 months, with a possible second-half reversal if conditions improve.
Price increases could be scaled back through schemes if deflation arrives. Management said dealer incentives were adjusted in line with the price hikes.
capex_capacity: Capex is described as normal and in line with prior years.
Powder and industrial liquid coatings are running at about 70-75% utilisation, with sufficient capacity.
Management aims to grow performance coatings at double digits, tied to infrastructure spend and the expansion plan outlined at the February strategy session.
Paint Plus retail format has replaced NXTGEN Shoppe and Shop-in-Shop, with about 250+ stores opened.
Paint-as-a-service is present in more than 250 cities; the Illuminati architect and designer programme in 45+ cities; the painter programme covers more than 1.2 lakh painters.
demand_pricing: Decorative demand has improved since November, with an uptick across the last five months. Management said there was no volume impact from the price hikes so far.

Management said the market has seen a constant uptick since November, and that new entrants and unorganised players also took price hikes in January and February. Management expects unorganised-player impact to show up over 3-6 months, mainly in low-end products such as primers.
Management said that for the Q4 mix improvement, new products were a large contributor and super premium emulsions performed well. Market share was gained in focused T2 and T3 towns across India.
Dealer incentives are typically higher in April as a stocking month. Management said they are being adjusted with the price increases, in line with normal industry practice.
Auto demand is strong, with OEMs reporting long waiting lists. Demand in infrastructure, appliances and other industrial segments is described as standard and normal.
Management said the company is not chasing market share at any cost, and is focusing on profitable growth.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q4 growth came from decorative versus industrial, and what was the volume and mix contribution in decorative?
qa_highlights.answer: Auto was up close to double digits and industrial overall was up slightly higher single digits. Decorative was mid-single digits or lower. Mix improved in both segments, which lifted contribution and profitability.

qa_highlights.question: What price hikes will sit in Q1, and how are B2B and industrial price negotiations going?
qa_highlights.answer: Decorative hikes were about 2% in March, then 5-6% each on 10 April, 21 April and 11 May, for a net higher-single-digit increase. Industrial channel prices were revised effective mid-April. OE price increases have been granted in part, with a slight delay in timing.

qa_highlights.question: Is 13-14% margin guidance for FY27 achievable, and does it assume current raw material costs persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated the 13-14% band as the endeavour, with an aim for the higher end. It expects raw material prices to stabilise after a temporary panic-driven spike, and believes conditions should improve in the second half.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses fall about 150 bps as a percentage of sales year on year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to a drop in fuel costs and fixed-cost leverage, plus ongoing cost and spend efficiency. It said there was no full-year true-up in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for decorative and industrial demand, and what would happen if crude corrects or stays high?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said auto demand is strong and deco trends are stable through April. If inflation persists, further price increases are possible. If deflation arrives, schemes would be adjusted first, with price cuts only if the softening is sustained. It said a crude price of about USD 100 would be manageable with current hikes.

qa_highlights.question: What share of sales do decorative projects and new businesses represent?
qa_highlights.answer: Decorative projects are about 10%+ of sales. New businesses (waterproofing, construction chemicals, wood finish) are also 10%+, slightly higher than projects.

risks_watch: Raw material inflation from crude and rupee depreciation. Management said price hikes will lag, so near-term margin pressure is possible; the sensitivity to 5-10% input cost increases was not quantified.
Management expects demand to be a wait-and-watch as the West Asia crisis and supply-chain disruption continue. A prolonged crisis could hit consumption through fuel and other costs.
Possible volume impact from price increases in the coming quarters, and inventory-led sales in April distorting secondary numbers.
Competitive intensity from new entrants and a delayed price increase among B2B and industrial customers.
Diwali timing is late this year, which could shift advertising and promotional spend across Q1 and Q2.
Other expenses fell about 150 bps as a percentage of sales YoY, which may not be sustainable if fuel costs normalise.
summary.management_tone: Confident on execution and pricing discipline, with management stressing profitable growth and deliberately avoiding market-share chasing. It was cautious and evasive on FY27 demand, auto price quantum, and the timing of raw-material relief, repeatedly calling forecasts "very difficult" and "a crystal guessing" exercise.

adds.what: Paint Plus retail format replacing NXTGEN Shoppe and Shop-in-Shop, 250+ stores opened

growth.why: Management reiterated a 13-14% margin band for FY27 as an endeavour, not a growth target; no explicit revenue guidance, with FY27 visibility described as "wait and watch" and growth backed mainly by price hikes (net high-single-digit decorative, plus industrial) rather than new capacity, with utilisation at about 70-75%.
